html: The Chemapho were a small band of the Kalapuya people of Oregon's Willamette Valley, probably living along Muddy Creek south of today's Corvallis. Like other Kalapuya bands, they gathered camas and acorns, hunted, and burned the valley grasslands to keep them open. Disease in the 1830s killed many. In 1855 the Kalapuya gave up the valley by treaty and were moved to the Grand Ronde reservation; their descendants belong to the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde. See also Santiam.
